_meta.author: Eduventure (original questions)
_meta.note: Upper secondary batch 1: Mathematics 10, Additional Mathematics 8, Physics 10, Chemistry 10, Biology 8, History 4. In review until approved in /admin. Contains answers: never imported by src/.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Select all the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0.
questions.explanation: Factorise: x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0, so x = 2 or x = 3.

wrong.c: Check: (−2)² − 5(−2) + 6 = 20, not 0. The signs flip when you read the roots from (x − 2)(x − 3).

questions.objective: Solve quadratic equations by factorisation.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary mathematics: quadratic functions and equations (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: n(A) = 12, n(B) = 9 and n(A ∩ B) = 4. Find n(A ∪ B).
questions.explanation: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B) = 12 + 9 − 4 = 17. The 4 shared elements would otherwise be counted twice.

mistakes.why: 21 counts the 4 shared elements twice; subtract n(A ∩ B).
Subtract the overlap only once: 12 + 9 − 4 = 17.

questions.objective: Use the formula for the union of two sets.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary mathematics: sets (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: What is 1101₂ (base 2) written in base 10?
questions.explanation: Place values from the right are 1, 2, 4, 8: 1×8 + 1×4 + 0×2 + 1×1 = 13.

wrong.b: 11 is 1011₂: the 1s are in different places.
wrong.c: 26 is 11010₂, every digit shifted one place left.
wrong.d: 4 is how many digits there are, not the value.

questions.objective: Convert numbers between base 2 and base 10.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary mathematics: number bases (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: True or false: the converse of "If x = 3, then x² = 9" is a true statement.
questions.explanation: The converse is "If x² = 9, then x = 3". It is false because x could also be −3.

wrong.true: A statement being true does not make its converse true. One counter-example (x = −3) is enough to show the converse is false.

questions.objective: Form and evaluate the converse of an implication.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary mathematics: logical reasoning (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: What is the gradient of the line 2y = 4x + 6?
questions.explanation: Divide everything by 2 to get y = mx + c form: y = 2x + 3. The gradient m is 2.

mistakes.why: Make y the subject first: divide the whole equation by 2.
3 is the y-intercept, not the gradient.

questions.objective: Find the gradient from the equation of a line.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary mathematics: straight lines (e.g. KSSM Matematik / SPM).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Where does the line y = 3x − 5 cross the y-axis?
questions.explanation: On the y-axis x = 0, so y = 3(0) − 5 = −5. The point is (0, −5).

wrong.b: 3 is the gradient, not the intercept.
wrong.c: This point is on the x-axis, and does not lie on the line.
wrong.d: (5/3, 0) is where the line crosses the x-axis.

questions.objective: Identify the y-intercept of a straight line.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary mathematics: straight lines (e.g. KSSM Matematik / SPM).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: y varies directly as x. When x = 4, y = 12. Find y when x = 7.

mistakes.why: 15 adds 3 to 12; direct variation multiplies by the constant k = 3.

questions.objective: Solve direct variation problems.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary mathematics: variation (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 5 / SPM).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Find the standard deviation of the data 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9.
questions.explanation: Mean = 40 ÷ 8 = 5. Squared deviations: 9, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 4, 16, which total 32. Variance = 32 ÷ 8 = 4, so the standard deviation = √4 = 2.

mistakes.why: 4 is the variance; take its square root.
5 is the mean, a measure of centre, not spread.

questions.objective: Calculate the standard deviation of ungrouped data.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary mathematics: measures of dispersion (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Match each set notation to its meaning.

right.text: Elements in both A and B
Elements in A or B (or both)

questions.explanation: ∩ (intersection) means in both. ∪ (union) means in either. A′ (complement) means everything in the universal set that is not in A.
questions.objective: Interpret set notation.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary mathematics: sets (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.prompt: Put these in order from smallest to largest.
questions.objective: Evaluate zero, negative and fractional indices.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary mathematics: indices (e.g. KSSM Matematik / SPM).

questions.subject: additional_mathematics
questions.prompt: Given y = 3x², find the value of dy/dx when x = 2.
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 2 × 3x = 6x. When x = 2, dy/dx = 12.

mistakes.why: 6x is the derivative; substitute x = 2 into it.
Bring the power down and reduce it by one: 3x² becomes 6x, not 6x².

questions.objective: Differentiate polynomials and find gradients.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary additional mathematics: differentiation (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tambahan Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: additional_mathematics
questions.prompt: Find ∫ 2x dx.
questions.explanation: Add one to the power and divide by the new power: 2 × x²/2 = x². Always add the constant c.

wrong.b: 2 is the derivative of 2x; integration goes the other way.
wrong.d: Divide by the new power 2: the coefficient becomes 1.

questions.objective: Integrate powers of x.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary additional mathematics: integration (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tambahan Tingkatan 5 / SPM).

questions.subject: additional_mathematics
questions.prompt: Find the value of log₂ 32.
questions.explanation: log₂ 32 asks: 2 to what power is 32? 2⁵ = 32, so the answer is 5.

mistakes.why: 16 is 32 ÷ 2; a logarithm asks for the power, not a division.

questions.objective: Evaluate logarithms.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary additional mathematics: indices and logarithms (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tambahan Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: additional_mathematics
questions.prompt: Find the sum of the first 10 terms of the arithmetic progression 3, 7, 11, …

mistakes.why: 39 is the 10th term; the question asks for the sum of the first 10 terms.

questions.objective: Find the sum of an arithmetic progression.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary additional mathematics: progressions (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tambahan Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: additional_mathematics
questions.prompt: For ax² + bx + c = 0, what does b² − 4ac < 0 tell you?

options.text: There are two equal real roots
There are two different real roots
One root is positive and one is negative

questions.explanation: The discriminant sits under the square root in the formula. A negative number has no real square root, so there are no real roots: the curve does not touch the x-axis.

wrong.b: Two equal roots happen when b² − 4ac = 0.
wrong.c: Two different real roots happen when b² − 4ac > 0.
wrong.d: The discriminant tells you how many roots, not their signs.

questions.objective: Use the discriminant to determine the nature of roots.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary additional mathematics: quadratic functions (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tambahan Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: additional_mathematics
questions.prompt: In how many different ways can 4 different books be arranged in a row on a shelf?
questions.explanation: 4 choices for the first place, 3 for the second, 2 for the third, 1 for the last: 4! = 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24.

mistakes.why: 16 is 4 × 4; once a book is placed it cannot be used again, so the choices go 4, 3, 2, 1.
10 is 4 + 3 + 2 + 1; multiply the choices instead of adding.

questions.objective: Count arrangements using factorials.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary additional mathematics: permutations and combinations (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tambahan Tingkatan 5 / SPM).

questions.subject: additional_mathematics
questions.prompt: In how many ways can 2 students be chosen from a group of 5 to form a team (order does not matter)?

mistakes.why: 20 is ⁵P₂, which counts each pair twice (AB and BA); divide by 2! because order does not matter.

questions.objective: Count selections using combinations.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary additional mathematics: permutations and combinations (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tambahan Tingkatan 5 / SPM).

questions.subject: additional_mathematics
questions.prompt: True or false: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 for every angle θ.
questions.explanation: On the unit circle, a point at angle θ is (cos θ, sin θ). By Pythagoras, cos²θ + sin²θ = 1² = 1, for every angle.

wrong.false: This identity comes from Pythagoras' theorem on the unit circle and holds for all angles, not just acute ones.

questions.objective: Recall the basic trigonometric identity.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary additional mathematics: trigonometric functions (e.g. KSSM Matematik Tambahan Tingkatan 5 / SPM).

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A car starts from rest and accelerates at 2 m/s² for 5 s. What is its final velocity in m/s?

mistakes.why: Multiply acceleration by time; do not add them.
25 m is the distance travelled (½at²), not the velocity.

questions.objective: Apply the equations of linear motion.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary physics: force and motion (e.g. KSSM Fizik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A 2 kg ball moves at 3 m/s. What is its momentum in kg m/s?
questions.explanation: Momentum = mass × velocity = 2 × 3 = 6 kg m/s.

mistakes.why: 9 J is the kinetic energy (½mv²), not momentum.
Multiply mass and velocity; do not add them.

questions.objective: Calculate momentum.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary physics: momentum (e.g. KSSM Fizik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure is force per unit area. 1 pascal = 1 newton per square metre (N/m²).

wrong.b: The newton is the unit of force.
wrong.c: The joule is the unit of energy and work.
wrong.d: The watt is the unit of power.

questions.objective: Recall SI units.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary physics: pressure (e.g. KSSM Fizik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A force of 100 N acts on an area of 0.5 m². What is the pressure in pascals?
questions.explanation: Pressure = force ÷ area = 100 ÷ 0.5 = 200 Pa.

mistakes.why: 50 is force × area; pressure divides force by area.

questions.objective: Calculate pressure.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary physics: pressure (e.g. KSSM Fizik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Select all the vector quantities.
questions.explanation: A vector has both size and direction. Velocity, force and acceleration all act in a direction.

wrong.b: Mass has size only, so it is a scalar.
wrong.d: Temperature has size only, so it is a scalar.

questions.objective: Distinguish scalar and vector quantities.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary physics: measurement (e.g. KSSM Fizik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A kettle connected to a 230 V supply draws a current of 2 A. What is its power in watts?
questions.explanation: Power = voltage × current = 230 × 2 = 460 W.

mistakes.why: 115 is V ÷ I; electrical power is V × I.

questions.objective: Calculate electrical power.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary physics: electricity (e.g. KSSM Fizik Tingkatan 5 / SPM).

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Which of these is a longitudinal wave?
questions.explanation: In a sound wave, particles vibrate back and forth along the direction the wave travels, making compressions and rarefactions. That is a longitudinal wave.

wrong.b: Light is an electromagnetic wave, which is transverse.
wrong.c: Radio waves are electromagnetic, so transverse.

questions.objective: Distinguish transverse and longitudinal waves.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary physics: waves (e.g. KSSM Fizik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Put these electromagnetic waves in order from shortest to longest wavelength.
questions.explanation: Gamma rays have the shortest wavelength, then X-rays, then visible light. Radio waves are the longest.
questions.objective: Order the electromagnetic spectrum by wavelength.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary physics: electromagnetic waves (e.g. KSSM Fizik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A wave has a frequency of 50 Hz and a wavelength of 2 m. What is its speed in m/s?
questions.explanation: Wave speed v = f × λ = 50 × 2 = 100 m/s.

mistakes.why: 25 is f ÷ λ; multiply frequency by wavelength.

questions.objective: Use the wave equation v = fλ.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary physics: waves (e.g. KSSM Fizik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Match each of Newton's laws of motion to what it says.

right.text: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
An object stays at rest or at constant velocity unless a resultant force acts on it

questions.explanation: First law: inertia. Second law: F = ma. Third law: forces come in equal and opposite pairs.
questions.objective: State Newton's three laws of motion.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary physics: force and motion (e.g. KSSM Fizik Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: How many protons are there in a carbon atom?
questions.explanation: Carbon's proton (atomic) number is 6, so every carbon atom has 6 protons.

mistakes.why: 12 is the nucleon (mass) number of carbon-12: protons plus neutrons.

questions.objective: Relate proton number to the identity of an element.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary chemistry: atomic structure (e.g. KSSM Kimia Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Find the relative molecular mass of carbon dioxide, CO₂. (Relative atomic masses: C = 12, O = 16.)
questions.explanation: CO₂ has one carbon and two oxygen atoms: 12 + 2 × 16 = 44.

mistakes.why: 28 is CO with only one oxygen; CO₂ has two.

questions.objective: Calculate relative molecular mass.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary chemistry: mole concept (e.g. KSSM Kimia Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: What type of bond holds sodium chloride (NaCl) together?
questions.explanation: Sodium gives an electron to chlorine, forming Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions held together by electrostatic attraction: an ionic bond.

wrong.b: Covalent bonds share electrons, usually between non-metals.
wrong.c: Metallic bonds hold atoms together inside a metal.
wrong.d: Hydrogen bonds are weak forces between molecules, not inside salt.

questions.objective: Explain how ionic bonds form.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary chemistry: chemical bonds (e.g. KSSM Kimia Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Select all the alkali metals (Group 1).
questions.explanation: Lithium, sodium and potassium are in Group 1. Each has one electron in its outer shell.

wrong.c: Calcium is in Group 2 (alkaline earth metals).
wrong.e: Chlorine is a Group 17 halogen, a non-metal.

questions.objective: Identify elements in Group 1.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary chemistry: periodic table (e.g. KSSM Kimia Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: True or false: diluting an acid with water raises its pH (moves it closer to 7).
questions.explanation: Adding water lowers the concentration of hydrogen ions. Fewer H⁺ ions per volume means a higher pH, closer to 7 (but it never becomes alkaline).

wrong.false: pH depends on the concentration of H⁺ ions. Dilution spreads them out, so the pH rises towards 7.

questions.objective: Relate pH to the concentration of hydrogen ions.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary chemistry: acids, bases and salts (e.g. KSSM Kimia Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: What are the products when zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Acid + reactive metal → salt + hydrogen: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂.

wrong.b: Salt + water comes from an acid reacting with a base, such as zinc oxide.
wrong.c: No oxygen is involved, so no zinc oxide forms.
wrong.d: Chlorine stays in the salt as chloride ions; no chlorine gas forms.

questions.objective: Predict the products of acid reactions.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary chemistry: acids, bases and salts (e.g. KSSM Kimia Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: How many moles are there in 36 g of water, H₂O? (Relative molecular mass of H₂O = 18.)
questions.explanation: Moles = mass ÷ molar mass = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 mol.

mistakes.why: 648 is 36 × 18; divide the mass by the molar mass.
0.5 is 18 ÷ 36; put the mass on top.

questions.objective: Convert between mass and moles.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary chemistry: mole concept (e.g. KSSM Kimia Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which gas turns limewater cloudy (milky)?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide reacts with limewater (calcium hydroxide solution) to form insoluble calcium carbonate, which makes it cloudy.
questions.objective: Recall tests for common gases.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary chemistry: qualitative analysis (e.g. KSSM Kimia / SPM).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Put these halogens in order of reactivity, most reactive first.
questions.explanation: Reactivity decreases down Group 17: fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine. Larger atoms attract an extra electron less strongly.
questions.objective: Describe trends in Group 17.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary chemistry: periodic table (e.g. KSSM Kimia Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Match each substance to its typical pH.
questions.explanation: Lemon juice is acidic (pH about 2), pure water is neutral (pH 7) and sodium hydroxide is a strong alkali (pH about 13).
questions.objective: Use the pH scale to describe acids and alkalis.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary chemistry: acids, bases and salts (e.g. KSSM Kimia Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Which molecule carries genetic information in cells?
questions.explanation: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) stores genetic instructions in the sequence of its bases.

wrong.b: ATP carries energy within cells, not genetic information.
wrong.c: Glucose is a sugar used for energy.
wrong.d: Haemoglobin is a protein that carries oxygen in red blood cells.

questions.objective: Identify DNA as the genetic material.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: inheritance (e.g. KSSM Biologi Tingkatan 5 / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: How many daughter cells are produced when one cell completes meiosis?
questions.explanation: Meiosis has two divisions, producing 4 daughter cells, each with half the original number of chromosomes.

mistakes.why: 2 daughter cells come from mitosis; meiosis divides twice.

questions.objective: Compare mitosis and meiosis.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: cell division (e.g. KSSM Biologi Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: What happens to most human enzymes at about 60 °C?

options.text: They are denatured and stop working
They work faster and faster without limit

questions.explanation: High temperatures change the shape of the enzyme's active site, so the substrate no longer fits. The enzyme is denatured.

wrong.b: Enzymes speed up as it warms only up to the optimum (about 37 °C for human enzymes); beyond that they denature.
wrong.c: Enzymes are proteins, and heat does not turn proteins into sugar.
wrong.d: Temperature has a big effect on enzyme activity.

questions.objective: Explain how temperature affects enzyme activity.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: enzymes (e.g. KSSM Biologi Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Select all the parts of the central nervous system.
questions.explanation: The central nervous system is the brain and the spinal cord. Everything else is peripheral.

wrong.c: Sensory neurones belong to the peripheral nervous system.
wrong.d: The heart is a muscular organ of the circulatory system.
wrong.e: The retina is a sense organ tissue in the eye that sends signals to the brain.

questions.objective: Describe the organisation of the nervous system.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: coordination and response (e.g. KSSM Biologi Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Put these in the order air passes through them when you breathe in.
questions.explanation: Nasal cavity → trachea (windpipe) → bronchus → bronchiole → alveolus, where gas exchange happens.
questions.objective: Trace the pathway of air in the respiratory system.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: respiratory system (e.g. KSSM Biologi Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: True or false: mature human red blood cells have no nucleus.
questions.explanation: Mature human red blood cells lose their nucleus, leaving more room for haemoglobin to carry oxygen.

wrong.false: Unlike most cells, mature human red blood cells have no nucleus; that space is used for haemoglobin.

questions.objective: Relate the structure of red blood cells to their function.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: transport in humans (e.g. KSSM Biologi Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Match each hormone to the gland that makes it.
questions.explanation: Insulin (lowers blood glucose) comes from the pancreas, adrenaline (fight or flight) from the adrenal glands, thyroxine (controls metabolism) from the thyroid.
questions.objective: Identify endocrine glands and their hormones.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: endocrine system (e.g. KSSM Biologi Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: What is the movement of water molecules across a partially permeable membrane, from a dilute solution to a more concentrated one, called?
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a partially permeable membrane, from where there is more free water (dilute) to where there is less (concentrated).
questions.objective: Define osmosis.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary biology: movement of substances across membranes (e.g. KSSM Biologi Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: history
questions.prompt: On what date did the Federation of Malaya gain independence?
questions.explanation: Malaya became independent on 31 August 1957, now celebrated as Hari Merdeka.

wrong.b: 16 September 1963 is when Malaysia was formed (Hari Malaysia).
wrong.c: 1 February 1948 is when the Federation of Malaya was set up, still under British protection.
wrong.d: 9 August 1965 is when Singapore left Malaysia.

questions.objective: Recall key dates in Malaysia's history.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary history: independence (e.g. KSSM Sejarah Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: history
questions.prompt: In which year was Malaysia formed?
questions.explanation: Malaysia was formed on 16 September 1963 from Malaya, Sabah, Sarawak and Singapore.

mistakes.why: 1957 is when Malaya became independent; Malaysia was formed six years later.

questions.objective: Recall key dates in Malaysia's history.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary history: formation of Malaysia (e.g. KSSM Sejarah Tingkatan 5 / SPM).

questions.subject: history
questions.prompt: Who was the first Prime Minister of Malaysia?
questions.explanation: Tunku Abdul Rahman, known as Bapa Kemerdekaan (Father of Independence), was the first Prime Minister.

wrong.b: Tun Abdul Razak was the second Prime Minister.
wrong.c: Tun Hussein Onn was the third Prime Minister.
wrong.d: Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad was the fourth (and later the seventh) Prime Minister.

questions.objective: Identify key figures in Malaysia's history.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary history: independence (e.g. KSSM Sejarah Tingkatan 4 / SPM).

questions.subject: history
questions.prompt: Put these events in the order they happened, earliest first.

options.text: The Federation of Malaya is set up

questions.explanation: Federation of Malaya (1948) → independence (1957) → formation of Malaysia (1963) → Singapore leaves (1965).
questions.objective: Sequence key events in Malaysia's history.
questions.alignment: Upper secondary history: independence and formation of Malaysia (e.g. KSSM Sejarah Tingkatan 4–5 / SPM).
